# Vault release cadence

@include 'alerts/enterprise-only.mdx'

Vault Enterprise and HCP Vault Dedicated 2.x and later follow this release
cadence. Vault Enterprise 1.x releases retain their existing maintenance terms:
eligible 1.19.x and 1.21.x releases can still receive backports under their
published coverage. Refer to [Vault Enterprise support](/vault/docs/enterprise/support)
for maintenance coverage and to [HCP Vault Dedicated version
management](/vault/cloud/versions) for service upgrade timing.

## Vault versioning

@include 'version-syntax.mdx'

## Feature release windows

Vault plans four feature release windows each year: minor releases in February,
August, and November, and a major release in May. The cadence applies from 2.x
onward. These windows are targets, not guaranteed release dates. Check the [release
notes](/vault/docs/updates/release-notes) for available releases.

## Feature and fix availability

Vault introduces features in the latest minor of the current major; it does not
backport features to earlier minors or older majors. For each major eligible for
fixes, subsequent bug and security fixes go to its latest minor and that minor's
patch releases.

With 2.2 available, 2.0.x and 2.1.x no longer receive backports; subsequent
eligible 2.x fixes go to 2.2.x. To receive those fixes, upgrade to 2.2.x and
keep its patches current. A major can remain eligible for fixes even when an
earlier minor within it no longer receives them.

You may still have access to technical support for an earlier minor under your
terms, but resolving an issue may require upgrading to a version with the fix.

## Final minor releases

The **final minor** is the last minor within a major. After the next major
becomes available, eligible fixes continue on the older major's final minor.
The final minor is not a new long-term support (LTS) release: it does not
restart or extend the major's Support Cycle-2 (SC2) lifecycle. The major's
support phase determines which fixes are available; Sustained Support provides
no new fixes. Refer to [Vault Enterprise
support](/vault/docs/enterprise/support) for coverage by phase.

The example shows the latest minor receiving patches within each major. Longer
lines illustrate the final minor after the next major becomes available; they
do not grant additional support time.

![Illustrative release timeline showing release branches and patch sequences, with 2.3.x, 3.3.x, and 4.3.x shown as the final minors of their respective majors.](/img/release-cadence-vault-docs_light.png#light-theme-only)
![Illustrative release timeline showing release branches and patch sequences, with 2.3.x, 3.3.x, and 4.3.x shown as the final minors of their respective majors.](/img/release-cadence-vault-docs_dark.png#dark-theme-only)

The timeline is illustrative: patch counts and endpoints are not release
commitments or support deadlines. For Vault Enterprise, check the applicable
Vault Self-Managed record in the [IBM Software Support
Lifecycle](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/lifecycle/) for lifecycle coverage
and any published dates. Do not infer missing dates from the timeline.

## Patch availability

Patch releases target a monthly cadence, but not every eligible major receives
a patch each month. Check the release notes for shipped fixes and consult
security advisories or Support for issue-specific guidance.

## Upgrade planning

Upgrade to the latest minor of your major to receive subsequent fixes. Once
that major's final minor is available, you can remain on its patch stream while
the major remains eligible for fixes. You do not need to adopt the next major
solely to retain the older major's remaining fix coverage, but features in the
next major require an upgrade.

If you plan feature upgrades once a year, we recommend targeting the final
minor of a major and keeping its patches current. Under the planned cadence,
that minor is expected to be `V.3.x` (for example, `2.3.x`). Confirm that it is
available and has enough remaining fix coverage for your upgrade plan.

Plan for any gap between the end of your installed version's fix coverage and
the availability of your target release. The release cadence does not define
supported upgrade paths; check the [upgrade guide](/vault/docs/upgrade) for
more information and test before upgrading in production.
